Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MediCore Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Mike Chen, CFO; and Lena Novak, Chief Technology Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MediCore Devices delivered solid results this quarter, driven by strong execution and continued demand for our innovative medical device solutions.

Today, I will cover four key aspects of our performance. First, our overall performance highlights and key achievements; second, hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates; third, gross margin trends and supply chain dynamics; and fourth, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. Mike will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Let's start with our overall performance highlights and key achievements, which really showcase another transformative period for MediCore in the medical devices space. As a leader in cardiovascular interventions and neuromodulation therapies, we've posted record results against a market seeing rising demand for minimally invasive procedures, AI-powered diagnostics, and value-based care shifts.

On the numbers front, for the full year to date through Q3 2024, we've hit net revenue of around $2.85 billion on a trailing basis, with organic growth at 20% year-over-year, marking our ninth straight year of double-digit expansion—well ahead of the medtech industry's 8-10% pace per IQVIA and Evaluate MedTech reports. Q3 revenue clocked in at $785 million, up 22% organically, powered by robust procedure volumes and share gains across the board.

Adjusted diluted EPS reached $4.15 year-to-date, up 25%, with Q3 at $1.28, beating our guidance. Adjusted operating margin stretched 320 basis points to 28.5%, thanks to leverage from high-margin consumables making up 72% of revenue, plus tight cost controls. Free cash flow hit $950 million year-to-date, up 30%, funding $450 million in buybacks, $300 million in R&D, and a 15% dividend bump to $0.35 quarterly.

By segment, Cardiovascular Interventions, 65% of revenue, jumped 24% organically to $1.85 billion. Standouts included our VitaFlow TAVR platform, with over 45,000 global procedures and 12% U.S. share in intermediate- and high-risk patients per CRT data. Electrophysiology grew 35%, led by the PulseSense AI ablation catheter, which cuts fluoroscopy by 40% and lifts first-pass success to 92%, edging out Biosense Webster and Boston Scientific.

Neuromodulation rose 12% organically to $650 million, highlighted by NeuroPulse 3.0 SCS for chronic pain, which earned FDA Breakthrough Designation and U.S. launch momentum. With 1,200-plus IDE trial patients, it shows 85% pain relief at six months—better than Medtronic's Intellis—and recurring revenue from replacements at 68%.

Global procedures grew 19%, beating benchmarks post-COVID elective rebound. U.S. sales, 62% of total, up 21% organically, aided by J&J stent co-promotion and CY2024 OPPS tailwinds for VitaFlow. EMEA, 22% of revenue, grew 16% with CE Mark for PulseSense driving 28% procedures in Germany and UK, taking share from Edwards. APAC, 12%, surged 32% with China TAVR doubling to 15,000 cases via MicroPort partnership, eyeing NeuroPulse NMPA approval mid-2025. LATAM and India added 8%, with neuro pilots gaining traction.

Achievements included eight FDA nods, like PMA for VitaFlow Prime with EchoGuide imaging slashing complications 25%. Reimbursement wins in Japan for TAVR and early EU MDR progress eased supply risks. R&D spend of $520 million—18% of revenue—launched 15 products, including AI RhythmGuard wearable for 96% AFib prediction with Apple Health integration, and BeatBot steerable sheath in coronary trials challenging Intuitive Surgical.

We closed the $1.2 billion NeuroDyn Therapeutics deal, adding SCS IP and closed-loop DBS for Parkinson's, eyeing $200 million revenue by 2026. Share gains hit 250 basis points versus Stryker, Abbott, Medtronic, via VitalCare platform covering 70% U.S. procedures with 15% better outcomes.

These set us up for 2024 challenges like IRA pricing and FX, but with TAVR low-risk expansion at 25% CAGR and neuromodulation ML shifts. Backlog at $3.1 billion up 28%, 75% U.S. coverage supports mid-teens growth and 29.5% margins.

Now, shifting to hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates, a critical leading indicator reflecting our commercial strength, especially for NeuroStim neuromodulation, PeriNav robotic navigation, and OrthoFlex joint implants. We track this via Salesforce CRM, 1,200 hospital contracts, and IQVIA/Komodo claims data.

In Q3, U.S. hospital adoption rose 18% year-over-year to 42% from 35.6%, our 11th straight double-digit quarter, despite flu-season procedure moderation and ortho payer scrutiny. Hospitals, 68% of $2.1 billion device revenue, hit 41% in spine/neuro procedures, up 16%, reclaiming 8 points from Stryker Mako via PeriNav 2.0's AI fluoroscopy cut of 37% per PROSPECT trial in The Lancet Neurology.

ASCs stole the show, with adoption up 52% to 31% of eligible procedures, now 22% of U.S. placements from 14%. Volumes leaped 41% on CMS 2024 OPPS expanding outpatient knees to 60% coverage. OrthoFlex's 15-minute implant time versus Zimmer's 28 minutes won 65% ASC tenders.

U.S. led at 45% hospital/35% ASC adoption, with VAC expansion to 420 sites including Cleveland Clinic. Europe at 28% hospital, gaining post-CE Mark with 22% in German/UK spine via Fresenius bundles. China up 39% to 19% hospital via Mindray JV, tapping 28% ASC CAGR per Frost. India at 14%, countered by low-ASP FlexLite.

Initiatives like PeriNav Connect cloud at 92% connectivity boost ASP to $14,200/spine case; FlexGuide catheters cut infections 44%, ASC pull-through 27%. Sales reps hit 112% quota, REACH study shows 22% savings unlocking Vizient/Premier deals worth $180 million backlog. NeuroVance buy targets 10% Parkinson's lift.

We guide 20-25% full-year growth, ASCs at 45-50%, risks low with titanium dual-sourcing.

Next, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary. Gross margin is our operational leverage barometer amid GPO pricing, high-margin shifts, and input volatility.

Q3 GAAP gross margin hit 68.5%, up 210 bps year-over-year and 140 sequentially. Non-GAAP at 70.2% excluding $12 million NovaSurgical amortization—best since 2019, ahead of 69-70% guide.

Mix shift drove 180 bps: Cardiovascular at 42% revenue (up from 38%) with EchoFlow Pro TAVR and Synergy-like stents at $8,000 ASP, 78% margins offsetting ortho from MicroPort. Pricing added 90 bps: 4-5% U.S. electrophysiology hikes pocketed 85%; Europe limited to 2% on MDR; Japan 6% on neuromodulation.

Costs contained 100 bps inflation: resins/nitinol up 7%, hedged 70%; freight down 15% via Mexico nearshoring.

Supply chain strong: lead times 8-10 weeks from 20, on-time 97% from 82%. Diversified single-source to <15%; dual sterile/EtO with Steris; semis at TSMC Arizona/Infineon Malaysia for pumps.

North America inventory 7.2 months via Blue Yonder AI. Europe offsets outages via NovaSurgical in-house robotics. China localizes neurostents for 20% savings.

Ahead, $150 million capex for Galway Industry 4.0 cobots targets 300 bps gain; biologics integration; ESG scorecards up yields 12%. Q4 margins 69.5-70.5%, supporting 15-18% op margins.

Finally, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains, key to our margin story in a tough macro. Our discipline drove 220 bps adjusted op margin expansion to 24.8% despite structural heart and neuromodulation investments.

Q3 SG&A at $682 million, up 3.2% reported/flat organic versus 9.1% cc revenue growth to $2.62 billion—deleveraging 270 bps to 26.0% from 28.7%. YTD $1.98 billion or 26.3%, beating 27% target, on track for 25.5-26% full-year. CoreStream program delivered $75 million run-rate savings since Q4 2023 launch.

Selling (65%) up 2.8% to $443 million despite U.S. sales ramp for EvoHeart TAVR vs. Edwards Sapien/Medtronic CoreValve in $4.5 billion market; offset by 15% T&E cut via VR training like Intuitive's da Vinci.

G&A down 1% organically to $239 million: Oracle Fusion AI P2P cut AP cycles 22 days, $18 million WC/$12 million savings; UiPath RPA slashed FDA 510(k)/rebate hours 40% for UnitedHealth/CVS Aetna.

U.S. (58% revenue) to 27.2% from 29.5% via 12 distributor consolidations like Stryker ortho, saving $22 million on NeuroStim DBS Parkinson's sell-through. EMEA deleveraged 350 bps to 24.1% with Dublin shared services for 14 countries, digitizing HTA dossiers cutting consulting 28% in Germany/France.

APAC up 12% absolute but to 22.8% from 25.1% with China hires for VisionPro OCT amid MicroPort da Vinci surge, Manila outsourcing at 35% lower costs.

CoreStream eyes $100 million more by 2025: AI sales optimization for 10-12% productivity; zero-based budgeting/DSO<55; $30 million NeuroVance synergies.

Q4 at 25.5%, offsetting inflation/FX for 12-15% EPS growth in $600 billion medtech.

I'll now turn the call over to Mike for a review of our financial results.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex outlined so comprehensively, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter. To recap key metrics: Q3 revenue of $2.62 billion grew 9.1% on a constant-currency basis, with full-year organic growth tracking toward mid-teens. Gross margins expanded as detailed, and SG&A deleveraged meaningfully.

Profitability was robust, with adjusted operating income up double-digits and EPS growth at the high end of expectations. Balance sheet remains solid, with $950 million free cash flow year-to-date supporting capital returns and R&D. For Q4, we guide revenue growth of 10-12% organic, gross margins to 69.5-70.5%, SG&A at 25.5% of revenue, and adjusted EPS of $1.30-$1.35. Full-year outlook holds at 12-15% EPS growth amid our efficiency programs.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Mike. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, good morning. Alex, could you expand on the ASC adoption momentum for OrthoFlex and PeriNav? How sustainable is the 52% growth given CMS shifts and competition?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, John. The ASC shift is a structural tailwind, with CMS OPPS enabling 60% outpatient knees, and our OrthoFlex's quick 15-minute implants giving us a clear edge—65% win rate in tenders. PeriNav 2.0's 37% radiation reduction per PROSPECT data has driven 41% volume surge, now 22% of placements. Sustainability comes from VAC footprint at 420 sites, REACH study proving 22% savings for Vizient/Premier contracts, and rep embedding at 75% high-volume ASCs. We're guiding 45-50% growth, with NeuroVance adding DBS upside. Confident it's here to stay.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson:
Hi, thanks. Mike, on SG&A, the CoreStream savings are impressive—$75 million run-rate. Can you detail Q4 trajectory and risks from wage inflation or NeuroVance integration?

Mike Chen:
Thanks, Emily. CoreStream's $75 million YTD is on track for $100 million more by 2025 across AI territory tools boosting rep productivity 10-12%, zero-based budgeting with DSO under 55 days, and $30 million NeuroVance overlaps via footprint cuts. Q4 at 25.5% absorbs wage/FX via efficiencies like Oracle AI and UiPath RPA. U.S. distributor rationalization and EMEA Dublin hub de-risk it. Inflation in platinum-iridium or EU MDR is covered—discipline fortifies our moat.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good morning. Lena, on the innovation side, how is PulseSense AI and RhythmGuard positioning us against Biosense and Apple ecosystem plays?

Lena Novak:
Hi David. PulseSense's real-time lesion prediction hits 92% first-pass, 40% less fluoro, ahead in electrophysiology. RhythmGuard's 96% AFib prediction integrates Apple Health seamlessly, covering 70% procedures via VitalCare cloud for 15% better outcomes. Our $520 million R&D—18% of revenue—fuels 15 launches, BeatBot trials challenging robotics dominance, and NeuroDyn's closed-loop DBS. Pipeline insulates from pricing, targets TAVR low-risk and neuro ML optimization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Alex, supply chain looks resilient, but any Red Sea or semi risks lingering, and how does NovaSurgical vertical integration help?

Alex Rivera:
Lisa, we've de-risked materially—lead times 8-10 weeks, 97% on-time. Diversified semis to TSMC Arizona/Infineon, dual EtO/Steris, Mexico nearshoring cut freight 15%. NovaSurgical brings 60% robotic manufacturing in-house, offsetting Europe outages. Galway $150 million Industry 4.0 cobots target 300 bps margins by 2026. Red Sea negligible with inventory at 7.2 months via Blue Yonder AI—no disruptions expected, supporting our guide.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question...

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to reiterate our confidence in the long-term growth potential of MediCore Devices. We are committed to delivering innovative medical device solutions that improve patient outcomes and create value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
